clue.text: Burnt offering, plain outrage

blocks.note: plain speaking is frank speaking
to outrage someone is to incense them

explanation.surface: A sacrifice goes up in flames, and the onlooker is openly scandalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burnt offering' suggests a sacrificed animal, but the resin burnt in temples is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic gum resin is burnt as incense in religious rites, one of the Magi's gifts.

clue.text: She and I fry fresh salmon etc, caught here

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made anew, so the letters before it are remade in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple cook fresh salmon and other fish, all landed at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fry' and 'fresh salmon' read as cooking, but 'fry' is fodder and 'fresh' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishery is a place or business where fish such as salmon are caught commercially.

clue.text: Article on setter shows spirit

blocks.note: the indefinite article
a gel is something that sets, read as set-ter

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about the crossword compiler reveals their character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler; here it means a thing that sets, as jelly or gel does.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a heavenly spirit, a supernatural being in religious belief.

clue.text: Bird I come to after Manx cat

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for cat loses its final letter

blocks.note: a pet name for a cat
taken as written
to come to after fainting is to wake

explanation.surface: Someone describes a bird reached after a tailless cat from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx is a tailless breed of cat from the Isle of Man, so the cat word is docked.
explanation.definitionFit: A kittiwake is a small gull of the open sea, named for its call.

clue.text: By all conclusions, when to raise hell — party season?

indicators.note: the conclusions are the ends of words, so only each word's final letter is used

blocks.note: the last letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Asking when the wild partying happens: is it the festive season?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as a playful description: Christmas is the season of office parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is another name for Christmas, the festive period of celebrations and parties.

clue.text: Risk grenade going off having grabbed pin, ultimately

indicators.note: a grenade going off explodes, scattering the letters into a new order
ultimately points to the final letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of pin

explanation.surface: A soldier pulls the pin of a grenade, which explodes and puts lives in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To risk something is to put it in danger, the verb meaning to jeopardise.

clue.text: Generous type, devil with tail up somewhat?

indicators.note: the last letter is lifted a little way up the word, set back inside it

blocks.note: the Devil's name

explanation.surface: A wicked character with a raised tail is oddly described as open-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: The devil's tail, his last letter, moves 'somewhat' up the word, two places rather than to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas brings gifts to children, the very model of a giving, bountiful figure.

clue.text: Crazy code-breakers?

blocks.note: first meaning: mad, in informal British use
second meaning: people who crack codes

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second meaning as a whimsical coinage: those who crack codes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for mad and also, literally, people who break ciphers or safes.

clue.text: Where ancient giant stood in more than one street, it's said?

indicators.note: it's said asks us to go by how the words are spoken, not how they are spelt

blocks.note: streets are roads

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where a huge ancient statue stood, apparently across several streets.
explanation.walkthrough: The ancient giant is the Colossus, a huge bronze statue of the sun god, one of the Seven Wonders.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colossus stood at the harbour of this Greek island city, one of the Seven Wonders.

clue.text: This grade remarkable, look at the score!

indicators.note: something remarkable is out of the ordinary, so these letters leave their usual order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exam result is so astonishing that someone cries out to view the marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' and 'grade' suggest exam marks; the score here is a piece of written music.
explanation.definitionFit: To sight-read is to perform music straight from the printed page without prior practice.

clue.text: Direction taken by old PM?

blocks.note: first meaning: a compass point
second meaning: Lord ..., British Prime Minister 1770-82

explanation.walkthrough: Lord North was the British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a cardinal compass point and the title of an eighteenth-century British premier.

clue.text: Cake: nearly all covered in cereal, flipped over

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
something covered in another thing sits inside it
flipped over turns the whole thing round so it reads the other way

blocks.note: a cereal grain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cake almost entirely coated in grain, then turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: AL goes inside RICE to give RIALCE, and the whole is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Better opportunity originally missed, in conclusion

definitions.note: read as a past-tense verb, bettered

indicators.note: the original, or first, letter is missed out
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a conclusion is an end
an opportunity is a chance

explanation.surface: A sports report: a better opening was squandered at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' must be read as the verb in the past, made better, to match the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enhanced has been improved or bettered, raised in quality or value.

clue.text: Follower, revolutionary in Vietnam's eyes

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie inside the following words
revolutionary means turning round, so the hidden letters read backwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A loyal follower looks like a revolutionary in the view of Vietnam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a Viet Cong guerrilla, but it is the signal to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-man is a sycophant who agrees with whatever a superior says, an uncritical follower.

clue.text: Little point in the sea launch for WWII flier

blocks.note: a spit is a narrow point of land running out into the sea
to launch a missile is to fire it

explanation.surface: A wartime scene of a small headland where an aircraft or rocket is launched.
explanation.definitionFit: The Supermarine Spitfire was the famous British fighter plane of the Second World War.

clue.text: Generous first dash of soda: without spirit?

indicators.note: a first dash is just the initial splash, the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: the opening letter of soda
an elf is a sprite or spirit
less means without, as in a suffix

explanation.surface: A barman pours a generous measure, just a splash of soda and no spirit in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like alcohol in the bar setting; it is a supernatural being.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfless person puts others first, showing unselfish generosity.

clue.text: Touch on clue one's nailed!

blocks.note: to finger something is to touch it
a tip is a hint or clue

explanation.surface: Someone touches a crossword clue and declares it solved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nailed' suggests a clue cracked; the definition means it has a nail on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of a finger carries a fingernail, so it is a part that is literally nailed.

clue.text: Prepare to catch with opener for Northants just out?

indicators.note: to catch is to hold something inside
the opener is the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: to prepare tea or beer is to brew it
and means along with
the first letter of Northants

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: getting ready to take a catch as the Northamptonshire opening batter is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: Northants is Northamptonshire, an English county cricket side; 'opener' and 'out' read as cricket terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand-new product has only just come out, fresh and unused.

clue.text: Article perhaps used in washing cotton sample

blocks.note: toile is a plain cotton or linen fabric
to sample something is to try it

explanation.surface: A piece of cotton fabric used as a test in the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: Toile is a fine cotton cloth, also a trial garment made up in cheap fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A toiletry is an item such as soap or shampoo used for washing and grooming.

clue.text: Upping routine, critical for country

indicators.note: in a down clue, upping sends the word upward, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: a rut is a dull routine
key means crucial or critical

explanation.surface: Raising one's routine is said to be crucial for the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey is the nation straddling Europe and Asia, with its capital at Ankara.

clue.text: Agreement during Whitsun is ongoing

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A deal reached over the Whitsun holiday is still in progress.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitsun is the Christian festival of Pentecost, a British bank holiday weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means in complete accord, everyone together as one.

clue.text: Celebrity lacking in skill?

blocks.note: lacking means not having
able means skilled

explanation.surface: A famous person who turns out to have no talent at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, 'not able' means lacking skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable is a famous or important person, a dignitary or public figure.

clue.text: Denying tiger fun proves foolish

indicators.note: something foolish is out of its right mind, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Refusing to play with a tiger turns out to be the sensible course.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuting a claim means rebutting it, disproving or rejecting it as false.

clue.text: Main part of body thus stuck under rock

indicators.note: in a down clue, stuck under places the first piece beneath the second

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky outcrop on a hill
so means in this way, thus

explanation.surface: A climber's body is trapped beneath a boulder.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, excluding the head and limbs.

clue.text: Little point claiming extra power for dictator

indicators.note: claiming means laying hold of, so one piece takes in the other

blocks.note: a dot is a tiny point
extrasensory perception, a supposed extra mental power

explanation.surface: A tyrant seizing additional power on the smallest pretext.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a ruler with absolute power, a tyrant or autocrat.

clue.text: Edge raised on gold dish from India

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised sends the word upward, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: a lip is an edge or rim
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A gilded serving plate from India with a raised rim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like a plate in the surface; it means a prepared food.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is a spiced rice preparation cooked in stock, popular in Indian cuisine.

clue.text: Lug rocks, ending on Salisbury Plain

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so the letters are jumbled
the ending is the final letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of Salisbury

explanation.surface: Hauling stones across Salisbury Plain, as the builders of Stonehenge did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' joins Salisbury Plain, the chalk plateau home to Stonehenge, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain describes someone not good-looking, unattractive, a polite term for unlovely.

clue.text: Fluff English, reading, writing and arithmetic, bagging zero

indicators.note: bagging means putting into a bag, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the three Rs of basic education
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A school report: muffing English and the basics, and scoring nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, the basic school skills.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluff is to bungle, and a fluff is a blunder or mistake.

clue.text: Dark individual in suit in entertainment venue

blocks.note: the dark is night-time
a club is a single card of the suit of clubs

explanation.surface: A shady figure in a business suit at a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Individual in suit' looks like a man in a business suit; it is one playing card from a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a late-opening venue offering music, dancing and drinks.

clue.text: Tree certainly not tidy around end of December

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes about another
end of points to the final letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: no way means certainly not
the final letter of December
spruce means neat and tidy

explanation.surface: A refusal to tidy up at the end of December, as Christmas decorations come down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at Christmas: this tree is the traditional British Christmas tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norway spruce is a European conifer, the traditional Christmas tree in Britain.
